key_insight: Jointly training subgrid-scale and wall closures inside a differentiable CFD solver lets the model learn coupled turbulence physics more effectively than fitting either closure alone.
engineering_relevance: This offers a reusable WMLES workflow that improves wall-bounded turbulence prediction, transfers across Reynolds numbers and meshes, and can reduce the need for case-specific tuning.
method: Hybrid neural--CFD framework with end-to-end backpropagation through the flow solver
Two composed closures: neural network + fixed differentiable layer for SGS and wall physics
Trained only on low-order statistics, then reused without retraining across multiple test cases
evidence_signal: On zero-pressure-gradient turbulent boundary layers, the method outperformed WMLES baselines across Re_theta = 600–6500, transferred to unseen grids/domains, and recovered mean-velocity and spectral trends not directly trained on.
watch_item: Because the gains rely on joint optimization inside a differentiable solver, implementation complexity and solver/mesh dependence may limit easy adoption in existing WMLES codes.
paper_title: Differentiable Hybrid Neural-CFD Modelling of Wall-Bounded Turbulence: Coupled Learning of Subgrid-Scale and Wall Closures
